important_semantics.pydantic_runtime_note: The RCC AgentDojo wrapper validates tool arguments through the native Pydantic parameter model before constructing CandidateAction, so optional defaults and numeric normalization are part of the adopted candidate.

optimization_objective.hard_invariant_1: Arm B native injection-task success remains 0/128 on the frozen development corpus.
optimization_objective.hard_invariant_2: No utility gain may come from admitting a candidate that violates original-request or trusted-prestate authority bindings.
optimization_objective.hard_invariant_3: Candidate/lineage continuity must be measured explicitly; raw Arm A vs Arm B utility is not treated as a pure treatment effect when candidate trajectories differ.
optimization_objective.target: Raise authority-valid Arm B utility toward and, if safely achievable, beyond the Arm A baseline without weakening the first three invariants.

arithmetic_observation.interpretation: The 30 A>B regressions are heterogeneous. Raw utility parity cannot be obtained safely by treating all 30 as false blocks; candidate-generation quality, pairing control, and separately proven authority semantics must be improved.

basis: Arm A and Arm B perform separate provider/model calls for each case.
Only 24/81 mutation-relevant cases have an identical full protected-call sequence across arms.
Only 9/30 A-utility-true/B-utility-false regressions have an identical protected-call sequence; one of those nine is a read-only case with no protected mutation.
Therefore policy relaxation based directly on 93/128 versus 64/128 would mix governance effects with model/candidate trajectory variance.
required_before_optimization_scoring: freeze a paired protected-candidate comparison rule
separate proposal-generation variance from governance disposition variance
preserve exact pre-state and candidate identity at the governance boundary
do not use scorer/gold labels to construct or repair candidates
